title: Factory Tour
paragraphs: After enjoying our bath, we took a leisurely rest, and the next morning arrived.
“For starters, let’s head over to the industrial complex where Takt and Shieldfreeden’s former CEO were jointly running their business.”

So, following Father’s instructions, we set out to tour Shieldfreeden’s development facilities for aircraft and firearms, as well as their paper production plant. Oh, of course, there’s a plane ready to take us to the nearest facility, and it’s been thoroughly maintained. It seems Shieldfreeden is desperately investigating to ensure that a terrorist attack like yesterday’s never happens again. Well, if anything does happen, we’ll be able to handle it.

So, after a few hours of whizzing along by plane, we arrived at our destination—the factory complex where the former Shieldfreeden CEO used to issue orders. We plan to use a portal for the return trip.
“I checked it out from the air… I don’t know how to put it, but it feels like a fantasy land.”
“Indeed.”

How should I describe it? It gives the impression of a townscape from the era when industrial pollution was at its worst, by Japanese standards. You can tell they’re making something using heavy machinery—it’s clanking and clanking away.

However… it doesn’t seem to be machinery, but rather golems and the like used in alchemy. If I had to describe it, I’d call it a “fantasy industrial zone.” The sky is colorful, and there’s no black smoke… but well, it’s somewhat similar. I’ve heard that members of the Takt faction explained this as evidence of their commitment to environmental protection.

Perhaps the ever-present rainbow gives off a clean image? There are also crystal-like objects emitting a sparkling light… In a way, you could say it’s a somewhat fantastical place. So, we’ll land by plane and head over to the factory for an inspection.
“Hmm, there’s a weird smell here.”
“Sakura, this is kind of gross.”
“It’s definitely not a place I’d want to stay in for long.”
“It’s gross!”
The Filolials are all furrowing their brows. As expected of the Filolials—their sense of smell is exceptional.
“The scenery is magical, but the air does seem a bit stale.”
“It seems like a good spot for a date, though.”

It’s not so foul-smelling that it’s unbearable; rather, I think you’ll find the atmosphere to be quite different from usual. After all, sharing that kind of unique atmosphere and setting is the secret to a successful date. Ah, I’d love to go to an amusement park with Filo-tan. However, it seems this place isn’t very popular with the Filolials. Let’s make a mental note that this spot is a no-go for when I eventually go on a date with Filo-tan.

“The fact that the idea of a date here was the first thing to come to mind… well, it just goes to show that Motoyasu-kun has quite a bit of experience, after all. But is it really okay to take a girl on a date to a factory?”

“Actually, not only does the factory have beautiful night views, but during the tour, there are plenty of opportunities to learn new things. Based on my standards, it’s just as solid a choice as an amusement park.”
“Huh…”

I should add, “Of course, in my world.” If I were the guy I was before coming to this other world—the kind who preferred intelligence and refinement—I probably would’ve included it as an option. When you think of dates, you usually picture amusement parks or movies, but what really matters is communication. Just as not all men are obsessed with video games or manga… Lady Filolial’s tastes vary widely too! Getting to know each other—that’s what a date is all about! Memories of the time I went on a motorcycle ride with Filo-tan during the last loop just came flooding back!
“It looks like a magical city, but it definitely doesn’t feel quite right. I wonder why.”
Panda is also looking around nervously. Maybe this little guy is sensitive to that sort of thing, too.

Just then, the head of the factory we’re inspecting this time came out to greet us. Apparently, he’s only been in the position for a few days. The previous factory manager apparently abandoned his post and fled the moment he learned of the defeat. Apparently, he was suspected of having ties to the remnants of Tact’s faction or something like that.

“Thank you very much for coming, the party of the Shield Heroes and Spear Heroes. This factory was operated under contract from Nelshen, the former representative of Shieldfreeden, and the felon Takt.”
“So you haven’t shut it down in response to the scandal?”

“Yes… If we were to close it down, the people in the surrounding area would lose their jobs, so we’ve been continuing to produce goods that are in demand… but we do plan to gradually phase that out as well.”
This is… a resource! That’s exactly what Father said last time!
“Demand, huh… I’m pretty sure firearms depend on your level, right? For low-level folks, aren’t they practically just toys?”

“The production and development of firearms that Nelshen was promoting have been temporarily suspended. We’re currently operating production lines for metal smelting, chemicals, paper, and the like. Also, at the request of the Shield Hero, we’ve instructed our employees to recreate conditions similar to those during Nelshen’s tenure.”
In other words, they’re trying to show things as they really are. I suppose that means they’re starting to develop a bit of a virtuous mindset.
“I see.”
“We’re currently operating the production lines that had been temporarily halted for the sake of the Heroes. As for the rest… I think you’ll understand once you see it. This way.”

With that, we set out to tour the Shieldfreeden factory. First, there are documents posted in the hallway explaining the history of how this factory was built. It looks like a memorial hall. Apparently, it wasn’t built as a temporary structure just because Father and his group were coming; rather, they intended to invite Shieldfreeden’s legislative representatives and create an open, welcoming space… or so they say. All in all, it even covers the history of Shieldfreeden.

“It says that those who strayed from Siltvelt’s policies migrated here in search of a new home, invaded this land where countless tribes clashed, and seized the territory while driving out the indigenous people… so the indigenous people are, you know…”

It depicts battles against rabbit-eared Demi-Humans portrayed as the kind of evil that must be vanquished. ...? I seem to recall seeing these rabbit-eared Demi-Humans somewhere before. Hmm… where was it again? I just can’t remember.

There’s a photo-like image displaying the attire of the defeated indigenous people as war trophies. It shows what looks like a bow. And… is that the moon? I suppose there are various cultures even among the Demi-Humans.
And so, the plant manager proceeds along the main—or rather, the intended—inspection route.

“Here, our nation, Shieldfreeden, handled everything from design to mass production of firearms that could serve as the next generation of weapons. Of course, ore mining was also conducted here, and explosives—which could be used even by those without Magic aptitude—were manufactured within this factory complex as well.”
“How should I put it… yeah, it really feels like I’ve come to a manufacturing plant.”
“Indeed.”
At first glance… judging from the steel production, firearms manufacturing, and development lines, it looks like a solid facility. It seems there’s a demand for this kind of thing, too.
“Well, up to this point, this is the ‘respectable’ route—the one we use to give presentations to visitors.”
“That’s a rather ominous way of putting it. So, you’re going to show us the ‘Darkness’ next… is that right?”
“Of course.”

I heard that the people on the observation tour belonged to Nelshen’s faction and were treated as senior workers. It’s said that since the faction was ousted, they’ve either already fled or been demoted. And so… the factory manager led us through a door at the far end of the tour route.
“And this is the real production line.”
“This is… hmm, are they just showing off?”

Father said this with a slightly exasperated look as he gazed into the depths of the factory. There, in stark contrast to the clean production line we’d seen earlier, was a rusty, dilapidated factory.

Clang, clang… it was a shoddy environment, as if it had been forged in an ancient blacksmith’s shop, now caked in rust. Employees with lifeless eyes were hammering or casting Magic on some sort of parts flowing by on a conveyor belt.
The employees’ faces looked haggard. There were Therianthropes mixed in as well… but their faces were so exhausted it was obvious at a glance.
“Ah, Foreman! That must be the Hero over there!”
A haggard worker looked up at us and flashed a cheerful smile.
“Yes, everyone, please do your best without overdoing it.”
“Yes, sir!”
Then, the employees looked our way, their eyes sparkling slightly as they bowed. Their expressions seemed to say, “We’ve stopped putting on a show now.” Hey, what’s going on here?
“Thank you so much for getting rid of Nelshen and Takt this time!”
“Ah, yes…”
“Please, we implore you to wipe out the remaining Takt loyalists!”

Father seemed taken aback—he clearly hadn’t expected to be thanked in a place like this—and replied with a troubled expression. True, under normal circumstances, these workers should be the ones in trouble now that Takt and his crew—their employers—had been defeated. So why do they look so happy?
“What do you think?”
“Well… ‘What do you think?’—what do you mean?”
“Thanks to you, the Heroes, we’ve been able to escape those harsh working conditions, and everyone’s full of motivation!”
“This!?”

Even Father looks genuinely surprised. It looks like they’re happily working in what seems to be the very definition of a “black company.” Suddenly, my knowledge of the original world and the previous loop came to mind. This is something I’d also recalled on the plane on the way to Shieldfreeden.
“If I recall correctly, Takt was a miser and a tightwad, wasn’t he?”

Apparently, he was the kind of person who hoarded money for no reason and refused to spend it even when he should have. By the way, it seems there are many reincarnated people like this—pointlessly stingy. Father was stingy, but he wasn’t the type to hesitate to provide funding where it was needed…

He himself used to say he placed great importance on resource management and productivity. Something about how the more money you spend, the bigger the things you can accomplish. I suppose that means the more you accomplish, the more wealth you generate. Well, this isn’t really my job, so I leave it all to Father.

“Yes… Although these were the paper manufacturing, firearms, and aircraft businesses promoted by Nelshen, their operations were funded by national tax revenue, and the majority of the profits were treated as operational funds for Nelshen and the Takt faction.”
“Using government tax money and pocketing the profits for themselves…”

“That said, this area was originally a mining region—one that was on the verge of decline—and thanks to the reforms we implemented, the industry flourished… However, since these were new ventures, the tax burden was very heavy, and the employees were forced to endure grueling working conditions. By the end, working hours of over 18 hours a day had become the norm.”
That’s beyond the pale. Is this what they call one of those notorious “black companies”?
“E-eighteen… w-were you okay?”
“Well… many people collapsed, but even in an environment like this, their quality of life had improved significantly, so…”
So they couldn’t escape, yet they had no choice but to endure a situation where they were being slowly strangled. It’s a terrifying environment.
“Above all, because this special stamina-Recovery drink developed by Takt was distributed, such an unreasonable work environment was even possible.”

A stamina-recovery drink, you say? From the looks of it… the container doesn’t seem much different from Magical Power Water or Soul-Healing Water. Still, just knowing he made it makes me view it with suspicion.
“Is that actually safe?”
“Of course not. According to the investigation, it’s so dangerous that its production has been banned.”
“I figured as much…”

Father is completely turned off by this. He’s saying that if you drank something like this, your body would be ruined within a year or something like that. Takt… in a way, he’s quite something. I can’t help but wonder how someone could stop seeing other people as human beings to that extent. Did he want money that badly?
By the way, according to the user, it apparently tastes good. They say it’s kind of addictive or something.
“Since I heard the Hero was coming to visit, I thought the country’s top brass might try to cover this up, so I kept the actual item. I’ll submit it to you, Hero, as evidence.”

Admittedly, given how things were going, it’s possible they would have covered it up so skillfully that it might never have reached Father’s ears. For a bunch of guys who were being used by Takt, they seem to be quite clever, don’t they?

Well then, I’ll analyze this using the alchemy Skills embedded in my spear. Hmm… It’s cleverly concealed, but there’s enough poison mixed in for even me to detect. It shows that it’s extremely addictive. It seems to restore a bit of strength and boost concentration, but it has the effect of drastically impairing cognitive function. This is practically a new type of poison.

Takt must have thought this made him a genius. Or perhaps he figured that with this potion, these guys would keep working forever? As expected, he’s fatally lacking any sense of consideration for his subordinates. I’ve decided to call this “Takt’s Special Stamina Recovery Drink” the “Corporate Slave Drink.”
“Although we’re in a situation where we have to pay a huge compensation claim to Siltvelt, even so, current wages have doubled, and working hours have been cut to one-third.”
“I-I see…”
Father nodded, his voice filled with disbelief.
“Just how extreme of a miser is he, anyway…”
Father muttered under his breath. It seems the conditions are already quite harsh even now. I wonder what it was really like back when the Takt crew was around.
“It’s surprising no one ever tried to break away, isn’t it?”
“Well… if anyone tried to do that, mysterious deaths and illnesses would happen frequently.”
“That definitely means they were being silenced, right?”
“Probably…”

It’s absolutely rotten to the core. It’s amazing people even gathered here under these conditions. Did they just figure there were endless numbers of people to exploit? It’s easy to imagine how they scattered scraps to the poor, forced them into backbreaking labor, and squeezed out massive profits.

“And… as for the profits and funds… at the same time Nelshen fled, the people involved also disappeared with the money, leaving this place with massive debts… Furthermore, since this factory’s production capacity has dropped to half of what it was at its peak, the revenue needed to restore our finances isn’t exactly…”
“Normally, if working conditions were improved and employee morale rose, productivity should recover somewhat—but if it’s still only half even after that…”
So the production conditions were already excessive and appalling to begin with. Or rather, it’s recovered to just half.

In other words, it’s a hopeless situation. Just how much money did the remnants of the Takt faction take with them when they fled? I had no intention of overlooking this to begin with, but depending on the amount, we’ll likely need to raise our alert level. Father began wringing his hands over the fact that they’ve now become a terrorist organization with enough money to rival a nation.
“I never imagined that letting those women escape when I took down Takt would have such lasting repercussions… I envy my counterpart from the other world.”

In the first world—and even more so—if I’d been able to take out Takt quickly, they wouldn’t have been able to flee with the money. In a sense… the damage might actually be even worse than in the first world. It’s a complete sinking ship.
“These are guns manufactured at our factory. We’d like to present them to you, the Heroes, as a memento.”
The factory manager is trying to hand a gun to Father with a smile. It might not be my place to say this, but I find that smile a bit off.
“No, seriously, I don’t need that. Don’t try to hand it over with a smile—it’s scary.”
This gun… as you’d expect from a reincarnated Takt, it resembles Earth’s firearms. I’m not that knowledgeable about them, but I’ve seen guns shaped like this in manga and such.
“A gun, huh? I’m interested in that. I just need to level up using the Hero’s power, right?”
The panda is taking aim with an assault rifle. I wonder if she even knows how to use it?
“It’s just a little small, though.”
Even for a giant panda, an assault rifle is considered small. Or maybe they’ll modify it for Demi-Humans and increase the caliber?
“For someone like you, Lasa, wouldn’t it be just right in your Demi-Human form?”
“That’s true… but I’m a little uneasy about using it in my Demi-Human form. I’ll think about whether to use it depending on the situation.”
“Hmm?”
“It’s a foolish weapon wielded by foolish people. We can fight just fine without such things.”
“Ahaha—bang bang, that sounds like fun!”
“Kou, you mustn’t treat guns like toys. If you use one, it definitely won’t end with it just being a toy.”
After all, Lady Filolial—whom I raised—has impressive stats. Even a pea shooter can pack quite a punch.

With that, we left the gun factory and headed straight to a paper mill… then a factory making parts for airplanes and other vehicles, and a car assembly plant… visiting one after another. It seemed the working conditions were similar at all of them; the workers told us that after having most of their earnings siphoned off, the owners had simply taken off. The only silver lining is that the workers seem to be on good terms with Father.
